source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ አውሥአኒ፡ ራጉኤል፡ ፩እምነ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ መላእክት፡ ዘሀሎ፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ዘርኢከ፡ ሩጸተ፡ †መዝኒ፡† መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ እሳት፡ ዘ*ይሰድድ፡ ውእቱ፡ ኵሎ፡ ብርሃናተ፡ ሰማይ።

translation.text: Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said to me, “What you saw—the running †məzni† toward the west—is the fire that drives all the lights of heaven.”[a]

footnotes.text: The daggered English token məzni is only a transliteration of the actual daggered መዝኒ. Its precise meaning and relation to “running,” “toward the west,” and “fire” remain unresolved, so this entire draft is held. Charles printed60 apparatus24 offers competing Greek/Ethiopic explanations; none is silently adopted. Actual Dillmann1865 col211 has related weighing, scales and a zodiacal name, but lexical proximity does not establish “measured course” here. The selected “drives” verb and “all” term are editorial emendations marked in apparatus25-26, not independently verified unanimous manuscript readings.
